01-title-menu: **A. Title-bar destination (macOS document title menu).** The window title reads 'Ledgerly Q4 review · 6 screenshots ⌄' centred in the title bar, like Pages' or TextEdit's document title; clicking it opens the destination menu (recent sessions with ✓ on the current one, Older Sessions…, New Session ⌃⇧N, separator, One-Shot). Nothing about the destination appears in the side column or the toolbar; the side column is only notes and the footer. Image 2 shows the menu dropping from the title.
02-toolbar: **B. Toolbar mode and scheme pop-up (Xcode / Preview).** At the right end of the toolbar, after Undo/Redo: a small grey segmented control 'Session | One-Shot' (Session selected with a grey fill and blue text, never a blue fill), then a pop-up button 'Ledgerly Q4 review (6) ⌄'. Window-wide choices live in the window's toolbar; the side column is untouched (notes and footer only). Image 2 shows the pop-up's menu open under it (sessions, Older Sessions…, New Session ⌃⇧N); One-Shot is the segmented control, not in the menu.
03-destination-row: **C. Destination row above the commit (the Save dialog's 'Where:' pop-up).** One row sits directly above Discard / Add to Session in the side column's footer: a label 'Add to' and a pop-up button 'Ledgerly Q4 review · 6 ⌄' filling the row. The notes column above holds only notes. Choosing One-Shot in that menu would turn the column into Beautify and the button into 'Copy ⌘↩'. Image 2 shows the menu opening upward from that row, next to the button it feeds. This is the evidence-backed recommendation: Fitts, Proximity, Common Region, CAP-5, WIN-5, ADR decision 3.
04-split-button: **D. Split primary button.** The primary button becomes a split button: 'Add to Session ⌘↩' plus a chevron segment '⌄' on its right edge; under the button a quiet caption 'Ledgerly Q4 review · 6 screenshots'. The chevron opens the destination menu (sessions, Older Sessions…, New Session ⌃⇧N, separator, One-Shot: Copy instead). No other destination control exists anywhere. Image 2 shows the menu opening upward from the chevron. Make it unmistakable that choosing a menu item only changes the destination and does not add.
